facts.text: Nasser Gholami, 47, of Brampton, charged by CBSA with firearm-related offences
Gholami is a Toronto Police constable with seven years of service
CBSA intercepted a U.S. parcel with two firearm suppressors at its Mississauga facility on July 23, 2026
OFSET searched Gholami's Brampton home Sept. 24, seizing three firearms, a suppressor, devices and ammunition
Gholami faces four counts: smuggling, importing, possession of prohibited devices and unsafe display of a firearm
Gholami is suspended with pay; chief intends to suspend without pay after mandated 60-day period
TPS says the CBSA charges are unrelated to his police duties
Next court appearance Nov. 5, 2026 at Brampton Courthouse
Allegations not tested in court; Gholami presumed innocent
Gholami has been released on conditions
Not confirmed that suspension without pay has taken effect; notification date not published
No reported cancellation or adjournment of the Nov. 5 court date

missed.text: CBSA announced the arrest and charges on Oct. 8, 2026; TPS confirmed Gholami's identity and suspension Oct. 10
CBSA's release did not name Gholami's employer
Charges laid under s. 159(1) Customs Act, ss. 103(1)(a), 92(2), 86(2) Criminal Code and s. 117(h) Firearms Act
CBSA release does not state whether Gholami has retained counsel or entered a plea; bail/release conditions not published
The Nov. 5 appearance is Gholami's first appearance
The duty-status and 'unrelated to his duties' lines are a single TPS statement repeated across CBC, CityNews, CP24/Star and Sun
